title.narrative: Ferghana Valley Water Resources Management Project

description.narrative: The Ferghana Valley Water Resources Management Project for Tajikistan objectives are: (i) to improve the capacity for increased irrigated agriculture productivity in the Ferghana Valley by improving land and water management, and (ii) to improve safety and regulation of the Kayrakum Dam and Reservoir. The project consists of the following components: Component 1) will finance design and works for rehabilitation of pumped and gravity irrigation and drainage systems serving some 30,000 ha of farm land in the Kanibodom and Bobojon Gufarov raions. Component 2) will fund (i) design and works related to rehabilitation of the Kayrakum Reservoir dykes in Kanibodom and Bobojon Gufarov raions, and (ii) technical studies, dredging and other equipment and instrumentations, and minor works to increase operational performance and improve management of the Kayrakum Dam and Reservoir. Component 3) will fund the necessary institutional capacity building for (i) establishment of Water Users Associations (WUAs), (ii) improving agricultural productivity and achieving more efficient water use patterns, and (iii) ensuring proper environmental impact mitigating measures. Component 4) will fund assistance to the central Project Management Unit (PMU) and to the regional Project Implementation Unit (PIU) established for project implementation.

The revised PDO is to assist the Recipient in: (i) increasing the coverage of drained and irrigated areas in Bobojon Gafurov andKannibodom raions, respectively; and (ii) strengthening the early warning system of the Kayrakkum dam as well as carrying out ageotechnical study for assessing the risks associated with said dam.

title.narrative: Forecast accuracy for available reservoir storage volumes and inflow/outflow volumes improved

comment.narrative: Forecasts are currently provided by the Scientific-Information Center of the Water Commission; the data can be also found onwww.cawater-info.net. Data is updated quarterly. The mission had discussed current status of the existing hydroposts on the upperside of Kayrakkum reservoir Okchar Hydropost and lower side of reservoir Kizilkishlak Hydropost with the Head of the SUEHydrometeorology service, Mr. Mahmad Safarov. Mr. Safarov confirmed that both hydroposts were rehabilitated in 1993 and 2003respectively. Currently information on the both posts is collected and reported manually. Being international hydroposts ontransboundary rivers information from these hydroposts is reported twice a day to the regional center.
